- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If supply net is strongly negative (e.g., < -15) and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward buffer.
- When bullish sentiment is low (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model often fails to anticipate sharp drops; apply lagged correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast 3–5 days after event.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overpredict mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–4% for each additional event beyond 15.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misreads trend direction; align forecast with dominant sentiment in last 5–7 days, not 18.
